social.title: Reds Game at Great American Ball Park
social.description: Baseball's oldest professional franchise, a riverside park with the steamboat smokestacks in centre field, and fireworks over the Ohio on Friday nights.
social.bonus: Get a photo with the smokestacks erupting after a Reds home run.

social.title: Dive Bar Night at Northside Yacht Club
social.description: A landlocked yacht club with a nautical joke running through the whole place, a punk-leaning jukebox, a patio and a burger people drive across town for.
social.bonus: Order the drink the bartender recommends without asking what is in it.

social.title: Rooftop at Braxton Brewing in Covington
social.description: A garage-born Kentucky brewery with a 5,000 square foot rooftop bar staring straight back across the river at the Cincinnati skyline.
social.bonus: Cross the Roebling Bridge on foot to get here rather than driving.

social.title: Liter Steins at Hofbräuhaus Newport
social.description: The first authentic Hofbräuhaus built outside Munich — communal benches, a live oompah band and liter steins carried four at a time.
social.bonus: Get the whole table to stand for the Ein Prosit toast.

social.title: Quarters and Pinball at Level One Bar + Arcade
social.description: Walls of cabinets and pinball on free play, themed cocktails, and no reason to look at your phone for three hours.
social.bonus: Set the night's high score on one machine and make everyone try to beat it.

social.title: FC Cincinnati Night in The Bailey
social.description: TQL Stadium's safe-standing supporters' end is the loudest room in the city — ninety minutes of unbroken singing, smoke and orange.
social.bonus: Learn one chant before kickoff and sing it properly, or don't bother standing there.

social.title: Bengals Sunday at Paycor Stadium
social.description: A full riverfront Sunday — tailgates on the lots, stripes on everything, and Who Dey going up from 65,000 people at once.
social.bonus: Find a tailgate that will feed you and talk your way into it.

social.title: Rooftop Pints at Rhinegeist
social.description: Twenty-five-odd taps, cornhole and ping-pong across a vast brewery floor in the old Christian Moerlein bottling plant, and a rooftop looking over Over-the-Rhine.
social.bonus: Win a game of cornhole on the roof before the sun goes down.

social.title: Pre-Prohibition Cocktails at Japp's Since 1879
social.description: An old wig shop on Main Street turned into a dark, tin-ceilinged cocktail room specialising in pre-Prohibition drinks, with gypsy jazz on Friday evenings.
social.bonus: Tell the bartender a spirit and a mood and drink whatever they hand you.

social.title: Patio Cocktails at Somerset
social.description: One of the largest patios in the city, strung with lights above McMicken, doing seasonal cocktails to a crowd that spills outside from the first warm evening onward.
social.bonus: Arrive early enough to claim a table, then hold it all night.

social.title: Beer Garden Evening at MadTree Oakley
social.description: Sixty-four taps, a ten-thousand-square-foot outdoor beer garden and a wood-fired pizza kitchen attached — the easiest group plan in the city.
social.bonus: Order a taster flight of things you would never buy a full pour of.

social.title: Apothecary Cocktails at Sundry and Vice
social.description: A Victorian apothecary set dressed as a cocktail bar — bitters in dropper bottles, tonics behind glass, and one of the best-made drinks lists in Over-the-Rhine.
social.bonus: Order something off the bitter end of the menu and finish it without wincing.

chill.title: Riverwalk at International Friendship Park
chill.description: A quiet stretch of riverfront east of downtown, full of public sculpture and almost nobody, with barge traffic sliding past a few metres away.
chill.bonus: Watch one full barge tow pass from end to end without moving on.

chill.title: Read the Afternoon Away at the Main Library
chill.description: The main branch downtown is one of the great American public libraries — vast, free, full of natural light and genuinely pleasant to spend a whole afternoon in.
chill.bonus: Pick a book at random from a section you would never normally browse and read the first chapter.

chill.title: Sunset from the Devou Park Overlook
chill.description: The classic postcard angle on Cincinnati — the whole skyline, both bridges and the river bend, from a hilltop in Kentucky.
chill.bonus: Get there before the streetlights come on and stay until they are all lit.

chill.title: Walk the Arboretum at Spring Grove Cemetery
chill.description: The second-largest cemetery in the country doubles as a accredited arboretum — 733 acres of lakes, champion trees and Gothic mausoleums you can walk for hours.
chill.bonus: Find the Dexter Mausoleum and stand in front of it long enough to notice how big it actually is.

chill.title: Ride Carol Ann's Carousel at Smale Riverfront Park
chill.description: A glass pavilion on the riverfront holding forty-four hand-carved figures, every one of them something distinctly Cincinnati — a flying pig included.
chill.bonus: Ride the flying pig. No negotiating.

chill.title: Look Through the 1845 Refractor at Cincinnati Observatory
chill.description: The oldest professional observatory in the United States still lets the public put an eye to its original Merz und Mahler refractor on clear public nights.
chill.bonus: Ask the astronomer on duty what they would look at if the dome were theirs alone.

chill.title: Afternoon on the Lawn at Washington Park
chill.description: Six acres of restored green in front of Music Hall, with an interactive fountain, a bandstand and a programme of free summer concerts.
chill.bonus: Stay for whatever is playing on the bandstand, even if you have never heard of them.

chill.title: Skyline View from Mt. Echo Park
chill.description: A 1900s hilltop pavilion on the west side with a straight-down view of the river valley and far fewer people than the better-known overlooks.
chill.bonus: Bring something to drink and stay through the whole colour change.

chill.title: Wander the Glasshouses at Krohn Conservatory
chill.description: An art deco glasshouse in Eden Park holding a rainforest, a desert and a twenty-foot indoor waterfall — tropical warmth on the worst Ohio day of the year.
chill.bonus: Find the orchid you would actually keep alive, and photograph it.

chill.title: Slow Coffee at Deeper Roots on Race Street
chill.description: A light-filled room beside Findlay Market built around a communal table and coffee roasted a mile away in the West End.
chill.bonus: Sit at the communal table and leave your phone in your bag the whole time.

culture.title: Free Afternoon at the Cincinnati Art Museum
culture.description: Sixty-seven thousand works across six thousand years, free to walk into, in a Romanesque pile on the edge of Eden Park.
culture.bonus: Pick the one painting you would steal and explain why to whoever you came with.

culture.title: Cincinnati Symphony at Music Hall
culture.description: One of America's oldest orchestras in a restored 1878 Gothic hall that is regularly named among the finest-sounding rooms on the continent.
culture.bonus: Get there early enough to walk the foyer and the grand staircase before the bell.

culture.title: Walk the Slave Pen at the Freedom Center
culture.description: The National Underground Railroad Freedom Center sits on the north bank of the river people crossed to be free, and holds an actual 1830s Kentucky slave pen inside it.
culture.bonus: Stand inside the pen for a full minute before you read a single label.

culture.title: Zaha Hadid's Urban Carpet at the Contemporary Arts Center
culture.description: Zaha Hadid's first American building — a stack of concrete boxes with a lobby floor that curls up the back wall, and rotating contemporary shows inside it.
culture.bonus: Walk the full zigzag staircase to the top before you look at any art.

culture.title: Cincinnati Shakespeare at the Otto M. Budig Theater
culture.description: A purpose-built thrust stage in Over-the-Rhine where no seat is more than twenty feet from the actors and a resident ensemble runs the full canon.
culture.bonus: Sit in the front row and hold a actor's eye contact for one full line.

culture.title: Stand in the Union Terminal Rotunda
culture.description: The largest half-dome in the Western hemisphere, lined with Winold Reiss mosaics — an art deco cathedral to rail travel that now holds the city's museums.
culture.bonus: Find the whispering arch and make it work.

culture.title: The Taft Museum in the 1820 Baum-Taft House
culture.description: A federal-era mansion downtown holding Rembrandts, Turners and Chinese porcelain in domestic-sized rooms you can actually look at things in.
culture.bonus: Sit in the garden afterwards and pick the room you would live in.

culture.title: Neon After Dark at the American Sign Museum
culture.description: A warehouse in Camp Washington packed with a century of American signage, including a full indoor Main Street that gets properly good once the neon is the only light.
culture.bonus: Watch the neon shop demonstration and try to follow how the glass gets bent.

8ball.title: Ride the Connector Loop End to End
8ball.description: Get on the free streetcar downtown and ride the entire 3.6-mile loop without getting off, then get off at whichever stop looked most interesting on the way round.
8ball.bonus: Whatever you do next has to be within two blocks of the stop you picked.

8ball.title: The Chili Parlor Showdown
8ball.description: Three-way at Skyline, three-way at Gold Star, three-way at Camp Washington — one night, one table, and a final ranking nobody is allowed to abstain from.
8ball.bonus: Write the ranking down before you leave the third parlor and send it to someone from Cincinnati.

adventure.title: Climb the Walls at RockQuest
adventure.description: Rope up in one of the region's longest-running climbing gyms, with tall lead walls, a bouldering cave and rental shoes for anyone talked into it at the last minute.
adventure.bonus: Top out a route one grade above whatever you claimed was your limit.

adventure.title: Walk the Bluffs at Shawnee Lookout
adventure.description: Follow the Miami Fort Trail along a bluff where the Great Miami meets the Ohio, past earthworks built two thousand years ago.
adventure.bonus: Stand at the overlook and pick out which river is which before checking.

adventure.title: Hit the Bays at Topgolf West Chester
adventure.description: Three tiers of heated hitting bays, microchipped balls that score themselves, and enough food and beer that nobody has to be good at golf.
adventure.bonus: Whoever scores lowest buys the next round.

adventure.title: Ride the Little Miami Scenic Trail from Loveland
adventure.description: Pick up the paved rail-trail in Loveland's bike-town centre and roll north through river bends and old railway cuts for as long as your legs hold.
adventure.bonus: Ride to the next town on the trail and eat something there before turning around.

adventure.title: Cross the Roebling Bridge on Foot at Golden Hour
adventure.description: Walk the 1866 suspension bridge John Roebling built as the prototype for Brooklyn, with the Cincinnati skyline at your back and Covington's riverfront ahead.
adventure.bonus: Make the blue deck grating sing — find the spot where passing tires hum a note and record it.

adventure.title: Climb the Mt. Adams Steps to Immaculata
adventure.description: Haul yourself up the public stairways that thread Mt. Adams to the 1859 Immaculata church on the summit, a pilgrimage route locals still walk every Good Friday.
adventure.bonus: Take the steps without stopping, then earn a drink at the top of the hill.

adventure.title: Ride The Beast at Kings Island
adventure.description: Spend a full day at Kings Island and give the night over to The Beast — still the longest wooden coaster on earth, and far better after dark.
adventure.bonus: Ride The Beast twice in a row: once in daylight, once after the floodlights come on.

adventure.title: Walk the Africa Trail at the Cincinnati Zoo
adventure.description: The second-oldest zoo in the country, built around 1875 aviaries and a botanical garden good enough to visit on its own.
adventure.bonus: Time your visit for a keeper talk and ask the keeper one real question.

adventure.title: Skate the Ice Rink on Fountain Square
adventure.description: An outdoor rink laid down in the middle of downtown every winter, circling under the Genius of Water fountain and the office towers.
adventure.bonus: Complete one lap skating backwards without grabbing the rail.

adventure.title: Swing Over the Ohio at Smale Riverfront Park
adventure.description: The porch swings on the riverfront face straight out at the Ohio and the Roebling Bridge — the best free seat in the city at dusk.
adventure.bonus: Claim a swing before sunset on a warm Friday. Good luck.

adventure.title: Cross the Shark Bridge at Newport Aquarium
adventure.description: Walk a rope bridge suspended inches above a tank of sand tiger sharks, then work back through the seamless acrylic tunnels underneath.
adventure.bonus: Stop dead in the middle of the bridge and count the sharks before you move on.

adventure.title: Paddle the Little Miami with Loveland Paddlesports
adventure.description: Put in on the Little Miami, a state and national scenic river, and drift a few green, heron-lined miles back toward Loveland.
adventure.bonus: Spot a great blue heron and name it before it takes off.

adventure.title: Hike the Twin Bridges Trail in Mt. Airy Forest
adventure.description: Drop into 1,400 acres of reforested hillside — America's first municipal reforestation project — on a trail that crosses two stone bridges deep in the woods.
adventure.bonus: Find the Everybody's Treehouse and climb to the top deck.

adventure.title: Zipline the Little Miami Valley at Ozone
adventure.description: Twelve lines strung 200 feet above the Little Miami at Camp Kern, one of the largest treetop canopy tours in the Midwest.
adventure.bonus: Go hands-free on the longest line and keep your eyes open the whole way.

adventure.title: Sunrise at the Ault Park Pavilion
adventure.description: Climb the steps of the 1930 Italian Renaissance pavilion before dawn and watch the light come up over the Little Miami valley with the city still asleep.
adventure.bonus: Bring coffee for whoever you dragged out of bed.

adventure.title: Mountain Bike the Devou Park Trail System
adventure.description: Ride the singletrack network stitched through the hills of Devou Park, where the climbs pay out in sudden gaps of Cincinnati skyline through the trees.
adventure.bonus: Clear one full climb without unclipping a foot.

foodie.title: Saturday Morning Crawl Through Findlay Market
foodie.description: Ohio's oldest continuously operated public market, where you graze your way past butchers, bakers and a dozen stalls instead of committing to one meal.
foodie.bonus: Buy one thing you cannot identify and eat it before you leave the market.

foodie.title: Three-Way at a Skyline Chili Counter
foodie.description: The other side of the chili argument: spaghetti, chili, a haystack of cheddar, and oyster crackers, eaten fast at a vinyl booth.
foodie.bonus: Settle it out loud — Skyline or Gold Star — and defend your answer.

foodie.title: Order a Five-Way at Camp Washington Chili
foodie.description: The James Beard America's Classic of Cincinnati chili — cinnamon-spiced, spaghetti-bedded, buried in shredded cheddar, served around the clock in a chrome diner.
foodie.bonus: Go at 2am and order the full five-way without looking at the menu.

foodie.title: Paella and Sherry at Mita's
foodie.description: Jose Salazar's Spanish and Latin American room on Race Street, built around paella, jamon iberico, ceviches and a sherry list worth working through.
foodie.bonus: Order a sherry you have never heard of and let the server explain it.

foodie.title: Liège Waffle at Taste of Belgium's Findlay Market Stand
foodie.description: The original waffle iron that started the whole operation, still pressing pearl-sugar Liège waffles inside Findlay Market.
foodie.bonus: Eat it plain first, before you let anyone put chicken on it.

foodie.title: Dinner at Boca
foodie.description: David Falk's flagship at Sixth and Walnut is the city's big-night-out room — luxe, theatrical and booked weeks deep for a reason.
foodie.bonus: Dress for it properly, and order the course you would normally talk yourself out of.

foodie.title: Goetta and Eggs at Eckerlin Meats
foodie.description: The Findlay Market butcher counter that has been grinding Cincinnati's German pork-and-oat goetta since 1852, crisped on a flattop and handed over the case.
foodie.bonus: Eat it standing at the counter like a local instead of taking it away.

foodie.title: Hand-Rolled Pasta in Sotto's Cellar
foodie.description: A candlelit basement under Sixth Street doing rustic Italian — hand-rolled pasta and wood-fired meats — in what feels like the best-kept room downtown.
foodie.bonus: Let the kitchen pick your pasta course instead of ordering it.

foodie.title: Pho and Tiki Cocktails at Pho Lang Thang
foodie.description: The Findlay Market pho counter that outgrew its stall and moved into a jewel-toned room on Race Street with a full bar and a dedicated broth kitchen.
foodie.bonus: Order the bun bo hue instead of the pho and see if you can finish it.

foodie.title: Black Raspberry Chocolate Chip at Graeter's
foodie.description: French pot ice cream made two gallons at a time since 1870, with chocolate poured in so it shatters into slabs rather than chips.
foodie.bonus: Find the single biggest chocolate chunk in your scoop and eat it last.

foodie.title: Pulled Pork and Jalapeño Grits at Eli's BBQ
foodie.description: A no-frills smokehouse on Riverside Drive where the pulled pork is the draw and the jalapeño cheddar grits are the reason people argue about the sides.
foodie.bonus: Get the grits as a side and refuse to share them.

foodie.title: Weekend Brunch at Sleepy Bee Cafe
foodie.description: A bee-themed breakfast room in Oakley doing sourdough pancakes, local eggs and a honey-forward menu that earns the queue out the door.
foodie.bonus: Order the Piggy Pancakes even though you said you wanted something healthy.
